answer: No, not as measured here. Among 30,399 inspected structures (16,244 destroyed, 53.4%), those nearer 'open land' (ground >100 m from any footprint) were destroyed LESS often, not more. With the direction fixed in advance (lower distance = riskier) AUC is 0.379 overall (Eaton 0.324, Palisades 0.409); i.e. farther-from-open-land AUC is about 0.62. Destroyed share rises from 44.7% in the nearest quartile to 71.7% in the farthest (Eaton 34% to 71%; Palisades 52% to 71%). The reversal persists within density strata. This does not show open land is safe: the feature cannot see wildland adjacency (all values >=100 m by construction, layer edge excluded) and the data are perimeter-selected, so edge buildings may simply not have been reached. Wind, embers, vegetation and hardening are not in the data. The rule was not supported, nor cleanly tested.
traps_or_caveats: Uninspected is not undamaged: 14,993 footprints with no DINS record (33%) and 41 Inaccessible were excluded, not counted as survivors.

Selection by outcome: the layer is footprints within 1/4 mile of the final perimeters and inspections cover structures the fire reached; results describe reached structures only, not fire-spread risk. Buildings just inside the perimeter edge (next to wildland) may have survived because the fire barely touched them, which would produce the reversal.
Perimeter distance was not used as a predictor (outcome leakage avoided).

'Open land' is a proxy: ground >100 m from any footprint in this layer, kept only >400 m inside the layer's convex hull. So every structure is >=100 m from it (bins 0-100 m are empty), and it cannot represent immediate wildland adjacency; it also includes parks, golf courses, reservoirs and bare ground, not just vegetation.

Edge exclusion removes the real WUI frontier: 1,281 structures (mostly Palisades, 1,165) lack a value; their destroyed rate was 0.43 (Eaton 0 of 116). Buildings outside the layer are unknown, so distances near its edge are unreliable.

Far-from-open-land structures are in dense urban cores (open distance correlates +0.27 with neighbor count; Eaton/Altadena was ember-driven urban conflagration), so the reversal is partly density/location confounding; still, it holds within density strata (AUC 0.36-0.52).
Wind, embers, vegetation type, roof material and defensible space are not in the data and not estimated; no causal claim. Destroyed rate is 53% so base rate is high and AUCs are modest.

Palisades vs Eaton assigned by centroid X < 380000 (UTM 11N); fire-specific results differ in magnitude (Eaton stronger reversal), and Palisades density/spacing features do rank in the expected direction (AUC 0.66-0.72) while Eaton's do not (0.48).
Slope from 3DEP 5 m DEM; 1,308 structures lack slope/open values near DEM tile edges.
Score_layer not run: this is an association check of a fixed feature against labels, not a spatial prediction layer; AUC computed directly in analyze.py.
